steps.title: The rule: Resource-oriented REST URLs and CRUD contracts

blocks.text: A URL path identifies a resource, and an HTTP method supplies the operation semantics rather than the path alone determining the action.

Model an item resource with a path parameter for its identifier and a collection resource without that item identifier. Specify retrieval with GET, collection-specific creation processing with POST, target replacement with PUT and removal with DELETE, preserving each method's semantics. A creation contract can use 201 with a Location identifying the created resource, while an absent item can use 404.

edges.label: On this item: GET retrieves; PUT replaces; DELETE removes.
POST collection creation: can use 201 + Location

blocks.alt_text: Make the orders collection and identified item visible as distinct resources. Annotate GET retrieval, POST collection creation processing, PUT item replacement and DELETE item removal, with 201 and Location /orders/42 for creation and 404 for an absent item.

steps.title: Trace the boundary: Resource-oriented REST URLs and CRUD contracts

blocks.text: Keep resource identity separate from the operation: /orders is the collection; /orders/{order_id} identifies an item. GET retrieves, POST processes collection creation, PUT replaces the target, and DELETE removes it. A creation contract can pair 201 with Location /orders/42; an absent item can use 404. Changing the method changes the semantics even when the item path stays the same.

steps.title: The rule: FastAPI application and path-operation declarations

blocks.text: Create a FastAPI instance and register a handler with @app.get("/path"), @app.post("/path"), @app.put("/path") or @app.delete("/path") for the intended method and path.

A path operation is the combination of an HTTP method and a path; handlers registered for different methods on the same path serve different operations. Routes are evaluated in order, so declare a fixed path before a conflicting parameterized path to prevent the latter from capturing it.

annotations.text: Review method, path, and declaration order together. GET and PUT on the item path register different operations. Declare /orders/current before a conflicting /orders/{order_id} route: the earlier parameterized route can capture the fixed path. A later fixed declaration does not automatically win.

created = "created"

retrieved = "retrieved"
replaced = "replaced"
removed = "removed"

def current_order(): return current
def retrieve_order(): return retrieved
def replace_order(): return replaced
def remove_order(): return removed

solution_files.content:
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()
created = "created"
current = "current"
retrieved = "retrieved"
replaced = "replaced"
removed = "removed"
@app.post("/orders")
def create_order(): return created
@app.get("/orders/current")
def current_order(): return current
@app.get("/orders/{order_id}")
def retrieve_order(): return retrieved
@app.put("/orders/{order_id}")
def replace_order(): return replaced
@app.delete("/orders/{order_id}")
def remove_order(): return removed

# Supplied registration inspector: no request handling by the learner.
def registration(index):
    routes = [r for r in app.routes if r.path.startswith("/orders")]
    r = routes[index]
    return [r.path, sorted(r.methods), r.endpoint.__name__]
